features.title: Medallion Pipelines
features.tldr: Two serverless Databricks DLT pipelines (dm-ethereum 24 tables, dm-app-logs 5) build the bronze/silver/gold medallion over S3 raw JSON.
features.summary: The DLT processing core of the platform. dm-ethereum reads Ethereum blocks, transactions and decoded calldata delivered to the S3 raw bucket by the external dd-chain-capture project; dm-app-logs reads Fluent-Bit NDJSON application logs. Both use Auto Loader for incremental S3 ingestion and run in the single Free-Edition Databricks workspace, with dev and hml as targets/catalogs. Triggers are currently paused and no update has run since the platform went idle.

features.title: AWS Resources
features.tldr: AWS inventory after capture retirement — S3, DynamoDB, Lambda, SSM, IAM, CloudWatch and Terraform state, each marked managed, orphan or residue.
features.summary: Single reference for every AWS resource this project provisions or depends on in sa-east-1: S3 buckets and path conventions, the DynamoDB single table and lock table (with two stale Terraform locks), the two Python 3.12 Lambdas and their triggers, the 27 shared SSM API-key parameters, IAM roles including the never-applied GitHub OIDC deploy roles, CloudWatch log groups, ECS/ECR and network residue, and the Terraform state key layout including the cross-project capture/ecr key.

features.title: CI/CD Pipeline
features.tldr: Seven GitHub Actions workflows with an informed environment gate, saved-plan apply and OIDC role-assumption — fully written but inert since April 2026.
features.summary: Describes the CI/CD control plane that deploys Terraform infrastructure, the Databricks bundles and the Lambdas: the 7 workflows present on develop and feature branches, the dependency-chain-aware environment gate with pre-gate plan artifacts and saved-plan apply, the intended four-role OIDC trust matrix, and the scripts/ci helper toolbox driven by stack_map.json. The OIDC roles were never applied and the AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_* variables do not exist, so CI cannot authenticate today.

features.title: Data Catalog
features.tldr: Unity Catalog inventory — 29 objects (12 streaming tables + 17 materialized views) across 7 schemas in the dev catalog of the Free Edition workspace.
features.summary: Canonical catalog of every Databricks table and materialized view produced by the DLT pipelines: schema descriptions, source lineage, column notes and key relationships. Reflects the live Free-Edition workspace, where the dev catalog holds 29 objects and popular_contracts_txs no longer exists.

features.title: Serving Layer
features.tldr: Four Lakeview dashboards over gold, plus a gold-export → S3 → Lambda → DynamoDB chain; alerts and the Genie space are declared but never deployed.
features.summary: The serving surface over the gold layer: four Lakeview dashboards (Network Overview, Gas Analytics, Hot Contracts, API Health) on the serverless SQL warehouse, the job_export_gold export to S3, and the S3-triggered Lambda that writes CONSUMPTION entities to the DynamoDB single table.

features.title: Capture Integration
features.tldr: Capture lives in the external dd-chain-capture project on a VPS; this repository only consumes the raw JSON it delivers to the S3 raw bucket.
features.summary: Data capture moved out of this repository to dd-chain-capture, which runs on a VPS and writes Kafka-Connect JSON to the S3 raw bucket under raw/mainnet-{blocks-data,transactions-data,transactions-decoded}/ with year/month/day partitions, plus Fluent-Bit NDJSON application logs. The bucket is the entire integration boundary: no queue, stream, shared library or network path. Field-name compatibility with the DLT Auto Loader schemas is not yet validated and the bucket has held no data since 2026-05-23.
